electrodynamics.goal: Maxwell found that waves of electric and magnetic field cross empty space at a rate set only by its permeability μ0 and its permittivity ε0. Write that rate c.
electrodynamics.name: Speed of light from the vacuum
electrodynamics.ask: Find c in units of 10⁶ m/s, with m = 1.2566e-6 H/m for μ0 and e = 8.854e-12 F/m for ε0.
electrodynamics.method: From the curl equations in empty space, each field obeys the wave equation with speed² = 1/(μ0 ε0).

magnetic_confinement.goal: A magnetic field B pushes outward on whatever carries the current that makes it. Write the pressure P it exerts, with the permeability of the vacuum μ0.
magnetic_confinement.name: Maxwell stress
magnetic_confinement.ask: Find P in megapascals for B = 13 T (m = 1.2566e-6 H/m for μ0).
magnetic_confinement.method: The energy stored in a field is B²/2μ0 per volume; pressure is energy per volume.

quantum_hall_effect.goal: With ν Landau levels filled, a sheet of electrons carries a Hall resistance R fixed only by the quantum of action h and the elementary charge q. Write R.
quantum_hall_effect.name: Von Klitzing constant
quantum_hall_effect.ask: Find R in ohms for the first plateau, n = 1 (h = 6.626e-34 J·s, q = 1.602e-19 C).
quantum_hall_effect.method: Each filled level carries a conductance of exactly q²/h, a topological (Chern) number times the quantum of conductance.

magnetars.goal: A core of radius R threaded by a field B collapses to radius r, keeping all the field lines through it. Write the field b it ends with.
magnetars.name: Flux freezing
magnetars.ask: Find b in units of 10⁹ T (u = 1e9) for B = 100 T, R = 7e8 m, r = 1e4 m.
magnetars.method: The flux Φ = Bπr² through the star is frozen into its conducting plasma, so B grows as 1/r².

magnetic_monopoles.goal: If a single magnetic charge g exists anywhere, the reduced quantum of action ħ and the elementary charge q fix its smallest value. Write g.
magnetic_monopoles.name: Dirac quantisation
magnetic_monopoles.ask: Find g in units of 10⁻¹⁵ Wb (u = 1e15) with h = 6.626e-34 J·s and q = 1.602e-19 C.
magnetic_monopoles.method: An electron carried round the monopole must come back with the same phase: q·g/ħ must be a whole multiple of 2π.

fusion_ignition.goal: A plasma of n deuterium-tritium pairs per cubic metre reacts at the rate n²/4·σ; each reaction gives an energy E. Write the power P each cubic metre makes.
fusion_ignition.name: Fusion power density
fusion_ignition.ask: Find P in MW/m³ (u = 1e6) for n = 1e20 /m³, s = 3e-22 m³/s (the reactivity near 15 keV) and E = 2.82e-12 J (17.6 MeV).
fusion_ignition.method: Half the ions are deuterium and half tritium: n/2 of each, so the rate per volume is (n/2)²⟨σv⟩.

nuclear_astrophysics.goal: Two nuclei of charges Z and z tunnel through their Coulomb barrier with an energy scale set by their reduced mass m, the speed of light c and the fine-structure constant α. Write that energy E.
nuclear_astrophysics.name: Gamow energy
nuclear_astrophysics.ask: Find E in keV (k = 1.602e-16 J) for two protons: m = 8.36e-28 kg, c = 2.998e8 m/s, a = 0.0073, Z = 1, z = 1.
nuclear_astrophysics.method: The tunnelling probability goes as e^(−√(E_G/E)); E_G collects every constant in the WKB exponent.

transuranic_synthesis.goal: N nuclei of a sample with half-life τ are left to wait a time t. Write how many n are left.
transuranic_synthesis.name: Radioactive decay law
transuranic_synthesis.ask: Find n for N = 1000 nuclei of californium-252 (T = 2.645 years) after t = 5.29 years.
transuranic_synthesis.method: Every half-life halves what is left: after t/τ of them, N is divided by 2 that many times.

nuclear_isomers.goal: Each nucleus of an isomer stores an energy E; a mole of them weighs M and holds N of them. Write the energy U each kilogram stores.
nuclear_isomers.name: Spin-trap capacity
nuclear_isomers.ask: Find U in GJ/kg (u = 1e9) for hafnium-178m2: E = 3.919e-13 J (2.446 MeV), N = 6.022e23 /mol, M = 0.178 kg/mol.
nuclear_isomers.method: Nuclei per kilogram are N/M; each gives E.

kilonovae.goal: Ejecta of mass M expanding at speed v stay opaque until their light can diffuse out through opacity κ. Write the time t its glow peaks, with the speed of light c.
kilonovae.name: Diffusion time of the ejecta
kilonovae.form: sqrt ( κ * M / ( 4 * π * v * c ) )
kilonovae.ask: Find t in days for M = 9.945e28 kg (0.05 suns), v = 3e7 m/s, k = 1 m²/kg (lanthanide-rich), c = 2.998e8 m/s.
kilonovae.method: Light escapes when the time to random-walk out (∝ κM/rc) equals the time since the blast (r/v): solve for t = r/v.

gamma_ray_bursts.goal: A jet moving at speed v beams its light forward into a narrow cone. Write the half-angle θ of the cone, with the speed of light c.
gamma_ray_bursts.name: Relativistic beaming angle
gamma_ray_bursts.ask: Find θ in degrees for a jet with b = 0.9999944 (its speed as a fraction of c, a Lorentz factor of 300).
gamma_ray_bursts.method: Aberration: light emitted at right angles in the jet's frame comes out at sin θ = 1/γ = √(1 − v²/c²) in ours.
